Double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) is a safe and accurate method for diagnosing small bowel disorders. While it may not be as widely used as other diagnostic techniques, DBE has been shown to be effective in detecting various abnormalities in the small intestine.

The completion of the provided retrieved matches provides insight into the use of DBE in different clinical scenarios. Here's a summary:

- DBE is safe and accurate for diagnosing small bowel disorders.
- Chromoscopy, biopsies, and treatment of lesions are all components of DBE that enhance its diagnostic accuracy.
- This method can be particularly useful for diagnosing recurrent bleeding vascular lesions such as diffuse lymphatic malformation (DL) in acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB).

In conclusion, double-balloon enteroscopy is a reliable tool for diagnosing small bowel disorders. Its ability to visualize the small intestine and identify various abnormalities makes it an effective method when performed by experienced endoscopists.

However, it's essential to note that DBE should not be relied upon as the sole diagnostic method, especially in equivocal cases. Clinical assessment remains a critical component of diagnosing appendicitis in children, as well as other conditions affecting the small intestine.

Overall, while there may be some variation in the effectiveness and safety of DBE compared to other diagnostic techniques, its accuracy and benefits make it a valuable tool for diagnosing small bowel disorders when performed by skilled endoscopists.
